title: Office Furniture Quotes: How to Compare the Real Installed Cost
metaTitle: Compare Office Furniture Quotes & Installed Costs | YOS
metaDescription: Compare office furniture quotes using a worked example and checklist for specification, delivery, installation, GST, exclusions and handover.
excerpt: A lower furniture price can become a higher installed cost. Compare the same specification and delivery scope with a worked example and a checklist you can send to suppliers.
body:
The fairest way to compare office furniture quotes is to put the same products, quantities and installation requirements against each proposal. Confirm GST treatment, delivery, assembly, placement and exclusions before comparing totals. A price for boxes delivered to a loading dock is not equivalent to an office ready for your team.

This guide is for business owners comparing furniture packages for a new office, relocation or workplace refresh. It separates furniture procurement from construction work, so you can see what each supplier has actually priced.

## What is the real installed cost of office furniture?

The real installed cost is the amount required to deliver the agreed furniture package, assemble it, position it and complete the agreed handover. Include any separately quoted services needed to reach that outcome. Keep optional upgrades separate and record unresolved costs rather than assuming they are free.

For a project requiring building works, electrical connections or data changes, those costs need their own agreed scope. Do not assume a furniture installer will perform regulated trade work.

## Start with one brief for every supplier

Give each supplier the same measured floor plan and furniture schedule. Record the people using the space, the intended use of each setting and the delivery location. Include access restrictions, existing furniture and the date the office needs to operate.

- Specify quantities, dimensions, product codes or comparable performance requirements.
- Confirm finishes, chair adjustment features, desk configurations and included accessories.
- Identify retained furniture and what must be moved, stored or removed.
- State whether you need assembly, room-by-room placement and packaging removal.
- Explain lift access, loading bookings, stairs and permitted working hours.
- Ask for current availability, quotation validity and a realistic delivery program.

If suppliers recommend different products, compare the differences explicitly. A useful alternative may deserve consideration, but it should not silently replace the original brief.

## Compare these items line by line

| Quote item | What to confirm in writing |
| --- | --- |
| Product specification | Same quantities, dimensions, finishes and required features, or clearly listed alternatives |
| Delivery | Destination, unloading point, access assumptions and any staged deliveries |
| Installation | Assembly, placement, fixing requirements and the agreed room layout |
| Site constraints | Lift bookings, stairs, restricted access and after-hours allowances |
| Existing furniture | Retention, dismantling, moving and removal included or separately priced |
| Packaging | Who removes it and what disposal arrangements are included |
| Services | Who handles power and data work, and what needs a separate trade quote |
| Handover | Inspection, defects, adjustments and the contact responsible for resolution |
| Warranty | Product-specific terms, exclusions, service process and applicable installation conditions |
| Commercial terms | GST, deposit, payment milestones, variation process and quotation expiry |

## Worked example: the cheaper supply price is not always cheaper installed

The following figures are invented to demonstrate the comparison method. They are not YOS prices, supplier quotes or market benchmarks. Both fictional proposals are assumed to cover an equivalent furniture specification; every amount shown is excluding GST.

| Scope | Proposal A | Proposal B |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Furniture supply | $12,000 | $13,200 |
| Delivery | $700 | Included |
| Assembly and placement | $1,100 | Included |
| Packaging removal | $200 | Included |
| Total excluding GST | $14,000 | $13,200 |
| GST at 10% for this example | $1,400 | $1,320 |
| Total including GST | $15,400 | $14,520 |

Proposal B has a higher supply price but a lower comparable installed total in this example. The difference is $880 including GST. That conclusion only holds if the specifications, access assumptions and included installation scope are equivalent.

If an access surcharge or installation item is still unquoted, mark the total as incomplete. Ask for the missing figure before treating the proposal as comparable. Do not invent an allowance and describe it as a confirmed supplier cost.

## Check how the furniture will reach the room

A correct room layout does not guarantee a straightforward delivery. Measure the loading route, lift, stairwell and doorways. Confirm whether large tables can be dismantled and whether there is room to assemble them safely.

Ask the supplier who books access and who coordinates with building management. For an occupied office, agree which areas can be taken out of service and whether the installation should happen in stages. Record any exclusions for waiting time, failed access or repeat delivery.

## Compare lead times and support, as well as price

Ask when the delivery clock starts: order acceptance, deposit, approved drawings or final finish selection. Separate stocked products from made-to-order items. A quote should explain which approvals the program depends on and what happens if the site is not ready.

Check warranty terms for the specific products rather than relying on a headline promise. Ask who investigates a defect, how replacement parts are sourced and whether any proposed assembly method affects coverage. Future parts and matching finishes should not be treated as guaranteed unless the supplier confirms them.

## Use this quote comparison checklist

Before you approve a package, check that you can answer these six questions:

1. Are the quantities and specifications equivalent?
2. Is the installed total complete and on the same GST basis?
3. Are delivery access and installation responsibilities agreed?
4. Are unresolved costs and optional upgrades identified?
5. Are approvals, lead times and payment milestones clear?
6. Is there a named contact for handover and defects?

## Frequently asked questions

### Should I compare furniture quotes including or excluding GST?

Use the same basis for every proposal and record both the excluding-GST and including-GST totals where applicable. Ask the supplier to clarify tax treatment. Whether your business can claim a GST credit is a separate accounting question.

### Does furniture delivery normally include installation?

Do not assume it does. Delivery, assembly, placement and packaging removal can be separate services. Ask each supplier to identify what is included for your site.

### Can I compare different furniture brands?

Yes, but first document material differences in dimensions, features, configuration, warranty and support. Compare suitability for the workplace alongside the total rather than treating different products as identical.

### What if a quote says installation is to be confirmed?

Treat it as an incomplete installed price. Obtain a site-specific installation scope and figure before comparing final totals or approving the order.
